findings.where: Lead paragraph above the stepper, every screen
findings.what: "A silicon diode drawn as a block, with holes on its P side ... and an example 10 Ω resistor." is a 30-word sentence with no verb. It sits above all 13 screens, including screens 1, 2, 10, 12 and 13, which show no loop and no curve. It also says the curve is "beside it", but at 360 px and at 1280 px the curve sits below. Replace it with one short true line, or drop it, so the lesson starts higher on a phone.

findings.where: Live line under the picture, screens 3 and 5
findings.what: The line under the picture chains clauses into sentences of 24 to 30 words, for example "The N side is positive, so the carriers are pulled back and the zone widens: almost no current flows, so the diode holds all 7.5 V." and "The zone is held thin and carriers stream across: the diode keeps 0.70 V, and the resistor takes the other 4.30 V of the 5.0 V supply." Split each into short sentences with one idea each.

findings.where: Junction drawing, screens 3 and 5 in reverse (360 light and dark moved shots, supply −7.5 V)
findings.what: The zone's dashed edge line falls on the outermost column of P-side minus signs. The edge is at x ≈ 137.1 and that column is at 137.5 ± 1.5, so those minus signs read as plus signs and the P edge shows "+ − −" instead of "− − −". That misleads on minus-on-the-P-side, the very charge screen 2's puzzle is about. The same overlap happens at the 50 V breakdown width. Snap the zone's half-width to a gap between columns, or draw the edge just outside the last ion column.

The explain carries 7 footnote markers. [^1] sits on "A diode lets current through one way and blocks it the other", which is not a rule or value he would look up. [^2] appears four times. The closing bold sentence carries two footnotes, [^2] and [^3]. Keep one [^2] on the 0.7 V, one [^3] on the PIV definition and the [^4] on the meter reading, and drop the rest.

"Predict first: what will the zone do..." is answered by the next lines on the same screen ("The empty zone thins"), so there is nothing left to predict. The lesson's predict field is null, though the brief promised predict before play. Make the prediction a quick pick before the drag, or move the explaining sentences into what shows after he moves the slider.

The screen goes from "The empty zone thins" straight to "Near 0.6 V carriers stream across". It never ties this back to screen 2's push-back: the supply works against the charge left at the junction and wins near 0.6 to 0.7 V. The explain has this link; the screen should carry it in one sentence, in place of a cut one.

"Below about 0.5 V almost nothing crosses. Near 0.6 V carriers stream across" states figures read off the example sketch as if they held for every silicon diode. Say "on this example curve", or tie the figures to the curve's ticks.

Breakdown is shown turning 50 W into heat, but no screen says what that does to an ordinary rectifier diode: it usually fails. One sourced sentence would finish the reason the PIV must sit above the supply, which screen 11 and the worked example lean on.

findings.where: Caption below the lesson, screens 1, 2, 4, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12 and 13
findings.what: "The curve is a sketch of an example silicon diode..." shows on screens that have no curve, for example the lamp and charger puzzles in the 360 and 1280 end shots. Show it only with the curve, or fold it into the curve's own note.

The analogy says the valve passes flow "for a small, fairly steady pressure loss", but the breaks say "A valve's pressure loss still climbs as the flow grows". The two contradict each other. Make the analogy say the valve's loss rises with flow, so the break about the diode's nearly flat drop is the true difference.
"Isolate, lock off and prove dead first." is repeated straight away by the first bullet, "Isolate, lock off, let any capacitors discharge, and prove dead." Keep the bullet and cut the repeat.

The brief promised the rule to use "diode check" for semiconductors and "resistance" for anything else, with the reason that a resistance range may not push enough to show the drop. It is missing. Add it as one line in the meter bullets.
